Welcome from the Headteacher
Our school is a vibrant, caring community where every child is nurtured to flourish academically, personally, and spiritually. From the moment you walk through our gates, you will see a joy for learning and an environment built on warmth and ambition.
We are a welcoming and inclusive school where pupils are happy and thrive; they have fun and a passion for learning.
Our latest Outstanding Ofsted Inspection Report states that the school has the ‘highest aspirations for all pupils' and that 'children flourish in this supportive and purposeful environment’.
At the heart of everything we do is our school mission: “Love one another as I have loved you” (John 13:34). Rooted in Catholic Social Teaching, our daily life is guided by core values of kindness, service, courage, and respect. While we are a Catholic school, we warmly welcome children of all faiths and none, and we regularly offer places across all year groups. Full details of the application process can be found on the Admissions page of the website.
While our website offers a glimpse into life at our school, nothing replaces seeing our community in action. I invite you to book a place at one of our upcoming Open Mornings to experience what makes us unique. Contact us today - we look forward to welcoming you to our school.

pageCache.pageTitle: St Elizabeth's Catholic Primary School - Our Patron Saint
pageCache.text:
Our Patron Saint
St Elizabeth of Portugal (1271–1336)
Early Life and Marriage
St Elizabeth of Portugal was born in 1271. She was a princess of Aragon (modern-day Spain), and she was named after her great-aunt, St Elizabeth of Hungary. As a child she was devout and compassionate. At just twelve years old, she was arranged to marry King Denis of Portugal, officially becoming the Queen of Portugal.
The Compassionate Queen and the Miracle of the Roses
Despite the pressures and politics of royal court life, Elizabeth prioritised helping the poor, sick, and vulnerable. She founded hospitals, orphanages, and shelters for the homeless, often using her own personal wealth to help those in need.
King Denis did not approve of her charitable works and forbade her to leave the castle to take food to the hungry. Elizabeth, however, carried on helping others in secret. On one cold, winter morning, while carrying bread hidden in her cloak to feed the poor, Denis confronted her and demanded to know what she was carrying. When she opened her cloak, the bread was miraculously transformed into fresh, blooming roses.
Elizabeth was a courageous peacemaker. When her husband and her son, Afonso, prepared armies to fight against each other, she bravely rode onto the battlefield between the opposing armies to stop the war. Her intervention restored peace and prevented a devastating civil war.
After King Denis died in 1325, Elizabeth gave all her wealth to the poor, and spent the remaining years of her life in simplicity and prayer in lay order, the Third Order Franciscans in Coimbra.
Elizabeth was canonized as a saint by Pope Urban VIII in 1625. She is often pictured with roses in her cloak and holding an olive branch, a symbol of peace.
A Model of Catholic Social Teaching
St Elizabeth is a wonderful example of Catholic Social Teaching for our school community to follow. She models the qualities that we aim to foster in our school, being:
A Peacemaker, resolving conflict through patience, courage, and empathy.
Kind and compassionate, helping those in need.
A leader through service, bringing out the best in others.
Our school community celebrates our patron saint on her Feast Day on 4th July with a Mass, whole school picnic lunch and concert.

Christ the Redeemer Catholic Education Trust
St Elizabeth’s is part of the Christ the Redeemer Catholic Education Trust.
For more information please visit the trust's website here - Christ the Redeemer Catholic Education Trust and see the message below from the CEO:
Welcome to the Christ the Redeemer Catholic Education Trust.
It is with great excitement and enthusiasm that I welcome you, as the founding CEO, to our new and quickly growing Multi-Academy Trust.
Our Trust consists of Catholic primary schools in Richmond and Kingston, with big educational ambitions for our children and young people.
It is anticipated that more Catholic primary schools will join our Trust, along with Catholic secondary schools.
As a family of schools, our vision is to be a beacon of exceptional Catholic education in which our young people flourish and fulfil their God-given potential. With Gospel values at the heart of our mission, we will cherish the unique nature of every member of our community so that our young people leave prepared and inspired to make a positive contribution to society.
Our teams will continue to work tirelessly to achieve this, collaborating across schools, united by the desire to deliver excellent educational outcomes.
Our teams will work together, sharing experience, sharing resources and sharing support. Our schools will be stronger by working together and collaboration will be at the heart of our culture.
We aspire to develop further partnerships with individuals and organisations to widen the impact of our Trust.
Please explore our website and do not hesitate to get in touch if you would like any further information.
John Conway CEO – Christ the Redeemer Catholic Education Trust

Catholic Social Teaching
At St Elizabeth’s, Catholic Social Teaching is central to how we put our faith into action. Rooted in the Gospels, Catholic Social Teaching is a set of principles that guides us in building a more just, peaceful, and loving world. It teaches us that every person has inherent dignity, that we are called to look out for the vulnerable, and that we have a shared responsibility to care for one another and our common home. By putting these values into practice we teach our pupils to think about the needs of others, challenge injustice and take action to build a better world for the future.
How Catholic Social Teaching is taught
Children are introduced to the principles of Catholic Social Teaching in all classes using both CAFOD resources and ‘Rooted in Love’ resources. We use the following Catholic Social Teaching principles:
Catholic Social Teaching forms an integral part of the Religious Education curriculum. In addition, we have a whole school Catholic Social Teaching focus each half-term where every class explores the same Catholic Social Teaching Principle at an age appropriate level.
Catholic Social Teaching is used in many subjects, History, Geography and English - it is not taught just in RE. Many of our assemblies feature Catholic Social Teaching where we discuss world events, the lives of inspirational people and how our faith challenges us to respond in a particular way.
Our charity work and action for justice
We were delighted to achieve the Oscar Romero Participator Award in March 2026 for our work in promoting Catholic Social Teaching in school. Below, you will see a selection of our charitable and Catholic Social Teaching activities.
Each year we support the following charities:
We raised £1,078 for CAFOD in 2025/26 through our non-uniform days and collections after our Advent Service and KS1 Nativity.
We have a close relationship with Small Steps, a local Richmond charity that provides specialist developmental support for young children with physical disabilities. Our Mini-Vinnies have organised ‘Wear Orange’ days and sponsored events to raise money for Small Steps. A group of our Mini-Vinnies were excited to visit Small Steps to see their work in action.
Greville House Care Home
Our KS1 choir sings carols at Greville House each year bringing joy to the elderly residents with their singing. Our children make Christmas cards for the care home residents each year.
The Mini-Vinnies and the Pupil Chaplains organise a Macmillan Cake Sale each year, using their baking skills to raise money to support those living with cancer.
Other charities we support are:
St Vincent de Paul Society
Catholic Children's Society
British Legion Poppy Appeal
Challenging Social Injustice
At times throughout the year our children learn about issues of social injustice and they are prompted to take action by writing letters to raise awareness.
The Y5 children were delighted to receive a response from the Prime Minister to the letters that they sent regarding the plight of refugees.
Our Y6 pupils were invited to watch a debate in the House of Lords by Lord Hunt of King’s Heath. This was in response to their letters asking for more action for climate change.

Weekly Update 25th September 2026
Read our newsletter to find out what has been happening in school this week and upcoming events ...
Dear Parents and Carers,
It has been fantastic to see so many parents attending the Class Information Sessions over the past couple of weeks. We are very appreciative of your support of our school and your child’s education and we look forward to working in partnership with you over this academic year.
A big thank you to all the Y5 and Y6s, who generously brought in cakes to sell at the Macmillan cake sale.
Thank you too, to the Mini Vinnies for organising the sale, which will support the charity’s important work, helping people living with cancer. We will update you when we have the final amount raised for Macmillan Cancer Support.
Diocesan Mass for the beginning of the school year
A group of Pupil Chaplains attended the ‘Beginning of the year Mass’ at St George’s Cathedral today.
Along with hundreds of pupils from schools across the whole of Southwark Diocese, they carried our school banner with pride and represented our school with maturity.
Well done to all the children who took part in the piano concert this evening. All children performed brilliantly in front of an audience of parents and siblings.
National Reading Quiz
Today, a team of 4 children took part in the southwest heat of the Junior National Reading Champions Quiz. This is a new national quiz for children aged 9-11 that has been launched as part of the National Year of Reading 2026.
The team showcased their love of literature and knowledge of books answering 55 questions on children's books and had a fantastic experience participating in this new quiz.
The scores were very close and the St Elizabeth's Team came fifth. They also won the "Best Cheerleading" award, winning a £25 book voucher for the school. This is awarded to the school with the best engagement and participation during the quiz (cheering each other on and showing the best team spirit as judged by the moderators).
Well done to Naia, Clodagh, Emma and Annabelle!
Movie Night for all children – Y6 Fundraiser
Next Thursday, 1st October, our Y6 parents are organising the first fundraiser of the year – a movie night! The film ‘Hoppers’ will be shown in the school hall from 6 to 8pm.
Tickets are £6 per child. This includes a slice of pizza, popcorn and a drink. Children can wear pyjamas or comfy clothes and they can bring a comfy cushion and their favourite teddy! It’s going to be a fun evening!
Save the date! PTA Bingo Night on Thursday 15th October .. more details to follow ..
CAFOD Family Fast Day
Friday 2nd October is CAFOD Family Fast Day. Children are encouraged to give up a snack on this day and donate the money saved to CAFOD. Children can bring their donation into school and we suggest £1 but welcome all donations. Alternatively you can make a donation to CAFOD at https://cafod.org.uk/give
Please follow the link to this week’s Wednesday Word for information and activities about this Sunday’s Gospel. https://www.paperturn-view.com/wednesday-word/good-news?pid=MTA101634&v=163.4
Children’s Commissioner’s National Children’s Survey: The Big Future
The Children’s Commissioner, Dame Rachel de Souza, is inviting all children throughout the country to complete a survey, called ‘The Big Future’. The ‘Big Future’ asks children about their lives, their experiences and their hopes for the future. The information gathered will be used to build a national picture of what matters to children today and to ensure their views are heard by Government. Please do consider completing the survey with your child at home. As well as being an interesting talking point for you as a family, it shows your child how they can contribute to democracy and have their voice heard. https://www.childrenscommissioner.gov.uk/thebigfuture

pageCache.text:
French
“One language sets you in a corridor for life. Two languages open every door along the way.”
At St Elizabeth's, we believe that learning a language is important for the social and economic future of all pupils. In order to form confident and enthusiastic language learners from a young age, our Modern Foreign Language (MFL) curriculum is founded on a combination of both linguistic and cultural components, which ensures that all pupils have a well-rounded knowledge of France and the French language.
We believe that immersing pupils in the French language is the most effective method of language learning. Repeated practice during weekly lessons with a specialist French teacher ensures that the language is heard and spoken regularly, consolidating children's learning and increasing their confidence. Learning through songs and stories, as well as celebrating key cultural, historical and religious events, maintains pupils’ excitement and curiosity towards language acquisition. The addition of higher-level vocabulary, more complex grammar and the refining of pronunciation constantly encourages pupils to master the language to the best of their abilities.
St Elizabeth’s follows our own scheme of work based upon the aims of the National Curriculum for Languages which is adapted to meet the needs of our own pupils:
As our pupils grow up to become global citizens, St Elizabeth’s attaches great importance to ensuring pupils promote the importance of tolerance and understanding of different cultures and languages in addition to their own. Our French curriculum’s focus on France’s historical, cultural and linguistic links with us and other countries plays a key role in encouraging and ensuring this endeavour.
